# Ribbon Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

### Shape

#### Description

A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab component with its default styling, borders, and spacing, only in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md)'s colours. Nothing adds to or takes away from a tab's own borders or margins, so a tab's label never shifts as tabs open and close. Along the top of the commands, a line in the colour of the tabs' own side borders runs from the far left, beneath the project indicator, to the side border of the first open tab, and on from that tab's other side border to the next open tab or the far right. An open tab meets the commands beneath it with no line between them, its side borders running straight down to where the line picks up again. There is no other line there, not even a faint one at a fractional display scale.
A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says more. Its tabs are, in order: Project, Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups. There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

#### Keyboard

<Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+5> opening Application. Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no tooltip.

#### Opening Several Tabs

Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open. Every open tab shows as selected.
The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side, in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with no divider between one tab's groups and the next, as between any groups. An open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the same height however many tabs are open.
Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between launches: the window always opens with only Project open.

#### Activity

The indicator and list of the [RunningActivityScope](../../../scope/running-activity/RunningActivityScope.md) sit just to the right of the project indicator, as it is beside the tabs or leading the collapsed ribbon.

#### Project Indicator

At the left end of the bar sits the [ProjectIndicator](../project-indicator/ProjectIndicator.md), a solid block the full height of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach it. There is no divider between it and what follows: the change of background is the edge. The activity spinner leads the tab bar, just after it.

#### Groups

Each group has its title in muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top) aligned along the left edge of the group naming what its commands have in common. The title sits on a strip with a slightly different background colour, at 12px, with generous padding either side of it within the strip, which runs the full height of the commands' area, with no padding above or below it, 8 pixels from the buttons beside it. The first group's strip sits flush against the left edge of the commands' area, with no space before it. Groups sit side by side, 8 pixels apart, with no divider between them: each group's title strip is what marks where it starts.
A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

#### Tabs

Each tab is a scope of its own, which says what groups and commands it holds, and what each command does.

##### Project

[RibbonProjectTabScope](project-tab/RibbonProjectTabScope.md)

##### Code

[RibbonCodeTabScope](code-tab/RibbonCodeTabScope.md)

##### Spec

[RibbonSpecTabScope](spec-tab/RibbonSpecTabScope.md)

##### Research

[RibbonResearchTabScope](research-tab/RibbonResearchTabScope.md)

##### Application

[RibbonApplicationTabScope](application-tab/RibbonApplicationTabScope.md)

#### Commands

A command button is one of two sizes, and each tab says which of its commands are which:

- full: its large icon above its label, exactly two slim buttons stacked tall
- slim: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label
- small: only in the collapsed ribbon: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label, and only as wide as they are

Buttons side by side are 8 pixels apart. Slim buttons side by side stack down instead, top aligned, two to a column, each column as wide as its widest button and each button as wide as its column; a third starts the next column, 8 pixels along. A full button always stands alone. A slim button fills only its column's width: nowhere does a button stretch to fill a row.
Every command starts from the top of its group, so the commands of a tab all start at the same line. A full button is always two slim buttons stacked tall, never shorter or taller, however much its icon and label would take, alone or beside any column.
Every button is square, with no rounded corners. Its background is clearly apart from the commands' area behind it, though still quiet: white laid a seventh of the way over that area in dark mode, and not quite half way in light mode, rather than a colour of its own, so it stays as far apart from a tinted body too, lighter in both modes, and more so while hovered; while pressed it darkens instead. An on or off setting, like dark mode, is a switch rather than a button, sitting in a block with a button's colour, as wide as a button of its size and as tall as the switch and its label need.
A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.
A command can be marked primary; each tab says which of its commands are.
A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip says why.

#### Height

The commands drive the height: the command area is as tall as the tallest column of the open tabs, padded 8 pixels above and below, and nothing more. Since no column holds more than two slim buttons, and a full button is two slim buttons tall, the tallest the command area gets is two slim buttons with 8 pixels between them, padded: 68 pixels, and never more. A tab whose tallest column is two slim buttons, or that has a full button, is taller than one of a single slim button, and a tab with no commands, which is only its "No commands yet" padded the same way, is the shortest of all. So switching tabs can change the command area's height, and the window beneath moves with it.
Every group is as tall as the command area, so the groups' title strips run its full height whichever tab is open.
There are 8 pixels of padding at the right end but none at the left: the first group's title strip starts right at the command area's left edge. "No commands yet" keeps 8 pixels from that edge. The groups' title strips are not padded, and run the command area's full height, with each title centred down its strip whatever that height is.

#### Collapsing

The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button at the right end of the ribbon, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1 (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the [UserPreferencesScope](../../../scope/user-preferences/UserPreferencesScope.md).
Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row led by the project indicator, the same solid block as beside the tabs, filling the row's height, with no divider after it, then the activity spinner, and then every primary command, from all of the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode as a small switch in a block only as wide as the switch and its label. Every one is only as wide as its own icon and label, 8 pixels from the next, whatever the tab it comes from calls it; a command that is slim in its tab doesn't grow to fill the row. They keep the order of their tabs, with a thin vertical divider between the commands of one tab and the next, and keep their tooltips and disabled states. The chevron sits at the right end of the row. Every control in the row, the chevron and the dividers included, is vertically centred in it.
When the spinner, commands, and dividers are wider than the room between the project indicator and the chevron, that stretch of the row scrolls sideways, as the expanded command area does. The project indicator and the chevron stay where they are, never scrolled away or squeezed, and nothing in the row shrinks to fit.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

Links in this document point at reference files. Read one when the work touches what it describes.

# Project Indicator

## Concept

### Pitch

Shows which project is loaded, at a glance, wherever it sits.

### Shape

#### Description

A solid block, the full height of wherever it sits, in its own colour: pure black in dark mode, darker than every surface around it, and a text input's background, the theme's well surface, in light mode. It has no border and no rounded corners. In it, a small folder icon, then the name of the project open through the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../../../scope/project-directory/ProjectDirectoryScope.md), which is its folder's name, in medium weight, vertically centred. The whole block is what is clicked, filling it edge to edge, square, and it highlights on hover.

#### No Project

While no project is open, as the [NoProjectStateScope](../../../scope/no-project/NoProjectStateScope.md) says, it reads "No project", muted, after the same icon, and has no tooltip.

#### Tooltip

While a project is open, its tooltip gives the project's full path.

#### Recent Projects

Clicking it, or pressing <Ctrl+`> (<Cmd+`> on macOS) anywhere in the window, opens a list of the recent projects of the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../../../scope/project-directory/ProjectDirectoryScope.md), up to five, newest first; doing so again closes it. Like the palette, the shortcut does nothing while an inset panel is open.
The list hangs flush from the indicator: its top edge is the indicator's bottom edge and its left edge the indicator's, at least 360 pixels wide. It is a solid block in the indicator's own colour, with no rounded corners, and a thin edge along its sides and bottom but none along its top, where it meets the indicator. While it is open, the rest of the window is dimmed as behind an inset panel, and the indicator stays undimmed above the dimming, so the two read as one.
At the top of the list, a filter field with a search icon takes the keyboard as the list opens. Typing filters the projects fuzzily, as the palette matches, by folder name or full path, the best matches first; with nothing typed, all of them show, newest first. <Up> and <Down> move a highlight through the rows, wrapping around, starting on the first row whenever the filter changes, and <Enter> picks the highlighted row.
Each project is a row with its folder name in medium weight above its full path, muted, after a folder icon, or a tick for the project open now. A busy project, of the [OpenProjectsScope](../../../scope/open-projects/OpenProjectsScope.md), shows a small spinner at the right end of its row, and beneath its path, muted, what is running in it, such as "Task running", "2 questions running", or "Building the spec", joined with a middle dot. A busy project is listed even when it is no longer among the five most recent, after them. Rows reach the list's edges, with no rounded corners, and highlight on hover. Picking a row, by clicking or <Enter>, closes the list and switches to that project, or just closes it for the one already open. Switching never stops what is running in the project switched from. Once switched, the chat input takes the keyboard, ready to write to the project switched to. Clicking the indicator, clicking the dimmed window, or <Escape> closes it.
The last row, beneath a thin divider, whatever the filter leaves, reads "Open Project…" after a folder icon, and closes the list and opens the [OpenProjectScope](../../../scope/project/open-project/OpenProjectScope.md).

#### Width

A name wider than 320 pixels is cut off with an ellipsis.

#### Following

It always shows the project open now: opening, creating, or switching to another project changes it straight away.

#### Busy Elsewhere

Every group is as tall as the command area, so the groups' title strips run its full height whichever tab is open.
There are 8 pixels of padding at the right end but none at the left: the first group's title strip starts right at the command area's left edge. "No commands yet" keeps 8 pixels from that edge. The groups' title strips are not padded, and run the command area's full height, with each title centred down its strip whatever that height is.

#### Collapsing

The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button at the right end of the ribbon, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1 (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the [UserPreferencesScope](../../../scope/user-preferences/UserPreferencesScope.md).
Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row led by the project indicator, the same solid block as beside the tabs, filling the row's height, with no divider after it, then the activity spinner, and then every primary command, from all of the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode as a small switch in a block only as wide as the switch and its label. Every one is only as wide as its own icon and label, 8 pixels from the next, whatever the tab it comes from calls it; a command that is slim in its tab doesn't grow to fill the row. They keep the order of their tabs, with a thin vertical divider between the commands of one tab and the next, and keep their tooltips and disabled states. The chevron sits at the right end of the row. Every control in the row, the chevron and the dividers included, is vertically centred in it.
When the spinner, commands, and dividers are wider than the room between the project indicator and the chevron, that stretch of the row scrolls sideways, as the expanded command area does. The project indicator and the chevron stay where they are, never scrolled away or squeezed, and nothing in the row shrinks to fit.

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

# Project Indicator

## Concept

### Pitch

Shows which project is loaded, at a glance, wherever it sits.

### Shape

#### Description

A solid block, the full height of wherever it sits, in its own colour: pure black in dark mode, darker than every surface around it, and a text input's background, the theme's well surface, in light mode. It has no border and no rounded corners. In it, a small folder icon, then the name of the project open through the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../../../scope/project-directory/ProjectDirectoryScope.md), which is its folder's name, in medium weight, vertically centred. The whole block is what is clicked, filling it edge to edge, square, and it highlights on hover.

#### No Project

While no project is open, as the [NoProjectStateScope](../../../scope/no-project/NoProjectStateScope.md) says, it reads "No project", muted, after the same icon, and has no tooltip.

#### Tooltip

While a project is open, its tooltip gives the project's full path.

#### Recent Projects

Clicking it, or pressing <Ctrl+`> (<Cmd+`> on macOS) anywhere in the window, opens a list of the recent projects of the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../../../scope/project-directory/ProjectDirectoryScope.md), up to five, newest first; doing so again closes it. Like the palette, the shortcut does nothing while an inset panel is open.
The list hangs flush from the indicator: its top edge is the indicator's bottom edge and its left edge the indicator's, at least 360 pixels wide. It is a solid block in the indicator's own colour, with no rounded corners, and a thin edge along its sides and bottom but none along its top, where it meets the indicator. While it is open, the rest of the window is dimmed as behind an inset panel, and the indicator stays undimmed above the dimming, so the two read as one.
At the top of the list, a filter field with a search icon takes the keyboard as the list opens. Typing filters the projects fuzzily, as the palette matches, by folder name or full path, the best matches first; with nothing typed, all of them show, newest first. <Up> and <Down> move a highlight through the rows, wrapping around, starting on the first row whenever the filter changes, and <Enter> picks the highlighted row.
Each project is a row with its folder name in medium weight above its full path, muted, after a folder icon, or a tick for the project open now. A busy project, of the [OpenProjectsScope](../../../scope/open-projects/OpenProjectsScope.md), shows a small spinner at the right end of its row, and beneath its path, muted, what is running in it, such as "Task running", "2 questions running", or "Building the spec", joined with a middle dot. A busy project is listed even when it is no longer among the five most recent, after them. Rows reach the list's edges, with no rounded corners, and highlight on hover. Picking a row, by clicking or <Enter>, closes the list and switches to that project, or just closes it for the one already open. Switching never stops what is running in the project switched from. Once switched, the chat input takes the keyboard, ready to write to the project switched to. Clicking the indicator, clicking the dimmed window, or <Escape> closes it.
The last row, beneath a thin divider, whatever the filter leaves, reads "Open Project…" after a folder icon, and closes the list and opens the [OpenProjectScope](../../../scope/project/open-project/OpenProjectScope.md).

#### Width

A name wider than 320 pixels is cut off with an ellipsis.

#### Following

It always shows the project open now: opening, creating, or switching to another project changes it straight away.
